title: Interview with Iris
summary: Kwame interviewed Iris, a teacher, in a newsroom interview.

qa_highlights.question: Tell me about a project that failed.
qa_highlights.answer: A mobile version nobody asked for cost six months and taught them to ask first

qa_highlights.question: How did you pay for the first year?
qa_highlights.answer: A small grant covered the equipment and weekend consulting paid for the rest

qa_highlights.question: Which tools do you rely on every day?
qa_highlights.answer: A notebook, a soldering iron and an old spreadsheet

qa_highlights.question: What would you tell someone just starting out?
qa_highlights.answer: Write down what you tried even when it fails

qa_highlights.question: What role does the community play?
qa_highlights.answer: Volunteers found most of the bugs

qa_highlights.question: Why does this work matter to you?
qa_highlights.answer: Small errors add up over years and become wrong decisions

quotes.speaker: Iris
quotes.text: It cost us six months and taught us to ask first.

quotes.speaker: Iris
quotes.text: The spreadsheet has survived four migrations.

quotes.speaker: Iris
quotes.text: Failed experiments teach you the most.

quotes.speaker: Iris
quotes.text: Without them we would still be guessing.

quotes.speaker: Iris
quotes.text: A tiny drift becomes a wrong decision.
